canonical_title: Exterior field of view - Multi-place air vehicles with side-by-side pilots
subject_group: 9.4.4 External visibility and transmitted visual indications

versions.title_at_revision: Exterior field of view - Multi-place air vehicles with side-by-side pilots
versions.text:
Standard: This standard applies to multi-place air vehicles with side-by-side pilots and anti-submarine and extended overwater patrol missions. The following is the minimum angles of unimpaired vision available to the pilot from the design eye position in TABLE XIII. TABLE XIII. Exterior FOV - Multi-place air vehicles with side-by-side pilots. At 0° through 30° azimuth, at least 17° down and 20° up. Between 30° and 70° left azimuth, external vision should increase from at least 17° down and 20° up to at least 35° down and 40° up. Between 70° and 110° azimuth, provide at least 35° down and 40° up. To the right of the pilot centerline the angular vision downward and upward may decrease from 17° and 20° specified due to the increased distance from the design eye position to the windshield. The transparent area should extend to 135° azimuth at eye level with vertical angles less than at 110°. At 90° azimuth, provide at least 70° downward with the pilot leaning outboard from their respective design eye positions. The entire transparent area between 20 degrees right and 30 degrees left is free of windscreen structure or posts. No windscreen post or structure exceeds 2.5 inches in width when projected onto a plane perpendicular to a line between the post or structure and the pilot design eye position. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analyze vision plots and verify that the total envelope (plus and minus 180 degrees in azimuth and plus and minus 90 degrees in elevation) from each crewmember’s design eye box provides the required clear vision areas as described in the standard. Vision plots are completed for each pilot’s position for all their primary operations. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
  (1) Demonstrate in flight that the external FOV allows the pilots to perform all their primary operations.
